correctness.rationale: Uniform insertion histories provide the exact all-subset survival product, verified by exhaustive rational enumeration. Gamma-ratio asymptotics give p_{n,i}=(i/n)^alpha(1+o(1)) and uniquely determine b_n=n^(alpha/(1+alpha)). The exact product yields uniform fixed-order factorization away from the origin, while Bernoulli inequality gives a globally summable subset bound and a small-origin control. Hence every compact-support Laplace functional converges to exp(-integral (1-exp(-f))x^alpha dx), establishing the full PPP and ordered-label Weibull/Gamma limits. 288 exact/numerical checker assertions passed; no infinite theorem relies on tests.

value.rationale: Earliest surviving intact birth-label is a canonical extreme statistic of the r-Stirling insertion process and of value-indexed plateaux, not an arbitrary slice. The theorem identifies a sharp multiplicity-dependent sublinear scale and the full limiting hierarchy, genuinely different from global plateau counts, macroscopic covariance data, and ordinary recursive-tree leaf ages. This exact all-r asymptotic description has independent mathematical interest as a rare-event boundary, without depending on a downstream theorem.
